Posterior Predictive Checks for a Joint Bernoulli Fit

Source: R/profile_ppc.R
profile_ppc.Rd

Observed-vs-model comparison at three levels – marginal (per class), pairwise (per class pair, all four RR/RS/SR/SS cells), and complete-profile (per full 2^D state) – plus a "not_computable" status for any group x check cell with too little direct support to evaluate at all. Nothing below the relevant min_* floor is silently omitted; it is reported with status = "not_computable" and NA numeric columns.

Usage

profile_ppc(
  fit_result,
  design,
  Y,
  ids,
  n_draws = 500L,
  min_tested = 10L,
  min_cotested = 10L,
  min_complete = 10L,
  min_count_group = 10L,
  min_partial_pattern = 10L,
  covariate_subgroups = NULL,
  min_subgroup = 10L,
  ci_level = 0.95,
  seed = 123L
)

Arguments

fit_result

List from profile_fit_joint_bernoulli (reads $fit).

design

List from profile_build_design (reads $stan_data: X, B, V).

Y, ids

The SAME Y matrix and ids data frame passed to profile_build_design (via profile_prepare_model_data) – the observed side of every comparison comes from these, not re-derived from raw data.

n_draws

Integer. Posterior draws used (subsampled if the fit has more). Default 500L.

min_tested, min_cotested, min_complete

Integer. Below these, a group x check cell is "not_computable" rather than evaluated. Default 10L each.

min_count_group

Integer. Below this many COMPLETE events in a group, the count_groups family is "not_computable" for that group. Default 10L.

min_partial_pattern

Integer. Below this many events sharing an EXACT partial test mask (in a group), that (group, mask) combination is skipped from partial_patterns entirely (never fabricated as a zero-support row – there are too many possible masks to report every absent one; only masks actually meeting this floor are listed, with every sub-profile of a LISTED mask reported, including its zero-count ones). Default 10L.

covariate_subgroups

Named list of vectors/factors, or NULL (default). Each vector must have length nrow(Y), in the SAME row order as Y/ids – e.g. list(specimen_type = ..., age_band = ...). When supplied, adds the covariate_subgroups table: the SAME marginal-level check as marginal, stratified by each named vector's levels instead of group (pooled across groups – these are prespecified clinical subgroup checks, not another hospital breakdown). Default NULL (the returned covariate_subgroups table has zero rows).

min_subgroup

Integer. Below this many tested events in a subgroup level x class cell, that cell is "not_computable". Default 10L.

ci_level

Numeric. Default 0.95.

seed

Integer. Draw-subsampling AND replicated-outcome simulation seed. Default 123L.

Value

A list of data frames:

marginal

one row per group x class: status, n_tested, n_resistant, n_susceptible, observed_resistance, expected_mean/lower/upper (= model_mean/lower/upper), predictive_mean/lower/upper, absolute_error, interval_contains_observed, predictive_interval_contains_observed

pairwise

one row per group x class-pair: status, n_cotested, n_RR/n_RS/n_SR/n_SS, observed_RR_prop etc., expected_RR_mean/lower/upper (= model_RR_mean/lower/upper, and _RS/_SR/ _SS), predictive_RR_mean/lower/upper, absolute_error (RR cell), interval_contains_observed, predictive_interval_contains_observed

complete_profile

one row per group x state (one "not_computable" row per group below min_complete, state NA): status, n_complete, state, empirical_count/frequency, expected_mean/lower/upper (= model_mean/lower/upper), predictive_mean/lower/upper, absolute_error, interval_contains_observed, predictive_interval_contains_observed

count_groups

one row per group x resistance-count 0..D (COMPLETE events only – total number of resistant classes): status, n_complete, count, empirical_count/frequency, expected_mean/lower/upper, predictive_mean/lower/upper, absolute_error, interval_contains_observed, predictive_interval_contains_observed

partial_patterns

one row per (group, exact test mask meeting min_partial_pattern, sub-profile over the TESTED classes in that mask) – the denominator is EVERY event sharing that EXACT mask, not events co-tested as part of a larger panel (that is pairwise's job) and not limited to one pair: an event tested on 3 of 5 panel classes contributes to exactly one mask's sub-profile breakdown here, at whatever order that mask is. Columns: status, mask (tested class names, "; "-joined), n_mask, sub_profile (R/S string over just the tested classes, in panel order), empirical_count/ frequency, expected_mean/lower/upper, predictive_mean/lower/upper, absolute_error, interval_contains_observed, predictive_interval_contains_observed. EVERY sub-profile of a listed mask is reported, including zero-count ones.

covariate_subgroups

empty (zero rows) unless covariate_subgroups is supplied; one row per (subgroup name, level, class), same columns as marginal but group replaced by subgroup_name/subgroup_level.

Details

TWO different quantities are reported for every evaluated cell, and they answer different questions – do not treat them interchangeably:

expected_mean/expected_lower/expected_upper (also exposed as model_mean/model_lower/ model_upper for backward compatibility)

the posterior mean and credible interval of the model's EXPECTED probability – an exact closed-form sum over state probabilities (the same softmax-over-states construction profile_build_design/ the Stan model use for the likelihood). This interval reflects PARAMETER uncertainty only: a model that is certain p = 0.5 reports a near-zero-width interval here, even though the actual count among replicated events would still vary.

predictive_mean/predictive_lower/ predictive_upper

a genuine posterior PREDICTIVE interval, simulated per posterior draw: for every event, one complete profile is sampled from that draw's joint state distribution, the event's ORIGINAL observation mask is reapplied (only classes actually tested in the real data contribute a replicated value), and the SAME replicated profile is used to compute the replicated marginal, pairwise, and complete-profile statistics for that event within that draw – so the joint dependence the model was fit to capture is preserved across all three levels, not simulated independently per level. This interval reflects BOTH parameter uncertainty and genuine outcome-level sampling variation, per Stan's own posterior-predictive-vs-posterior-expectation distinction (https://mc-stan.org/docs/stan-users-guide/posterior-prediction.html).

interval_contains_observed (unchanged from earlier versions of this function) checks against the EXPECTED interval, for backward compatibility with profile_release's rollup; predictive_interval_contains_observed checks against the PREDICTIVE interval – the two can disagree, and a cell that fails the tighter expected-probability check may still pass the (necessarily wider) predictive check.

This also avoids the confirmed defect in the J2-L four-cell-sensitivity experiment's fc_partial_specs() (grouping comparison rows by the observed outcome pattern itself, which makes "observed proportion" 1.0 by construction, not a real check): every "observed" count here – n_tested/n_resistant, n_cotested/n_RR etc., empirical state frequency – is a plain tabulation from Y against a FIXED category (a class, a pair, a state), never derived by matching each row's own label back to itself.
